To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the human brain predicts upcoming stimuli, (2) these predictions are represented as brain activity patterns, (3) these brain activity patterns are activated in anticipation of the predicted stimuli, and (4) these predictions are formed based on the statistical structure of the sensory information
the human auditory system is able to anticipate upcoming sounds, and that the anticipation is reflected in the brain’s response to the sound.
the human brain preactivates a template of its expected response to a stimulus, and that this template is used to detect and decode the incoming sensory information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the brain anticipates upcoming stimuli.
the question of how the human brain predicts and processes incoming sensory stimuli.
the mechanisms of prediction in human auditory perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is not only a passive receiver of sensory inputs but rather a highly active processor that prepares itself for the expected stimuli and thereby facilitates the perception of the world.
the human brain predicts sensory stimuli and prepares the brain to respond to them.
human auditory processing relies heavily on preactivation of a sound-specific brain activity pattern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human brain is a predictive system that anticipates upcoming sensory information by activating a template of its neural response.
the brain uses the prediction to preactivate a specific brain state, which is then used as a template for sensory processing.
the human auditory system relies on preactivation to predict sound.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human brain is not a passive observer of the world, but actively anticipates upcoming sensory input.
the human brain is not just a passive recipient of incoming sensory information, but actively anticipates upcoming stimulation.
the human brain is not a passive receiver but actively anticipates the incoming sensory information.
